data-model-approved.reason: ⚠️ SATISFIED 2026-09-03 AT THE THIRD ATTEMPT, and the two reopenings are the reason to trust this one more than the first. WHAT EXISTS: 5 runtime records — consent, kiln-project, kiln-session, model-compatibility, setup-transaction — each with a JSON Schema in `schemas/runtime/`, a per-record version, a declared location, and a committed-or-ignored classification a test compares against the code's own table. Validated through the existing Ajv layer (DEC-0033). ⚠️ THE COMPATIBILITY RECORD'S REQUEST PROFILE IS NOW BOUNDED BY CLASSIFICATION RATHER THAN BY HASHING: 31 scalar compat fields and 3 safely typed structures by value, with unknown keys refused at every depth; and 2 operator-authored records, plus non-empty samplingParams and non-authentication headers, recorded as CATEGORY NAMES ONLY and requiring a supplied non-secret declared identity — no identity, no cache. Authentication headers are excluded entirely and are not determinants, because rotating a key changes nothing about what the model can do. ⚠️ THE SECOND REOPENING WAS CAUSED BY MY OWN REPAIR. To keep unbounded members in the key without persisting them I digested the whole compat object, which would have written the SHA-256 of an operator's secret to disk — the exact credential-derived fingerprint this project's own schema documentation warns about two files away. Three defects, one pattern: a declarative guard trusted to cover more than it does. `propertyNames` covers one level; a regex describes a shape rather than canonicalising one; a digest bounds size, not sensitivity. ⚠️ THE COVERAGE TEST PROVES CLASSIFICATION, NOT SAFETY, and that limit is now written into the test itself. The digest defect passed a green version of that check, because a field classified as 'structured, covered by a digest' was classified and still wrong. What the suite adds now is the specific negative cases — the reported input among them — asserting that no value, no key name and no digest of either reaches the file. ⚠️ WHAT IS APPROVED IS THE SHAPE, NOT THE WRITER. No code writes these files yet; that is TSK-0026's work.
